clue.text: Dance music mostly performed before argument arises

definitions.note: the definition is a mass noun while the answer is a plural noun naming several such pieces

indicators.note: mostly means the synonym loses its last letter, keeping most of it

parts.note: to perform a concert is to give it, past tense gave

indicators.note: in a down clue arises means the word climbs, so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: a set-to is a brief quarrel or fight

explanation.surface: Some dance music was played just before a quarrel broke out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims GAVE to GAV; 'arises' turns SETTO upwards to OTTES.
explanation.definitionFit: Gavottes are old French dances and the tunes written for them, a common movement in Baroque suites.

clue.text: 24 down as member of trio, together with group of musicians

parts.note: Bach is one of the Three Bs of music, with Beethoven and Brahms, so here he stands for the letter B
together with is a plain synonym of and

explanation.surface: A composer joins two others in a trio and plays with a group.
explanation.walkthrough: The Three Bs is a traditional label for Bach, Beethoven and Brahms; as one of them, 24 down (BACH) supplies just B.
explanation.definitionFit: A band is a group of musicians playing together, from jazz combos to brass ensembles.

clue.text: Puzzle cryptically written by one finishing below

definitions.meaning: a puzzle or riddle, something baffling

definitions.text: cryptically written by one finishing below
definitions.meaning: the composer of the ... Variations, whose name is at 25 across, its last letter sitting right under this light

explanation.walkthrough: The 'one finishing below' is ELGAR at 25 across, whose final R lies directly below this entry; he wrote the Enigma Variations, whose hidden theme is itself a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or riddle, and Elgar's most famous work bears that title.

clue.text: See 22
Stupid person's variation on a theme by Dvorak, initially

indicators.note: a variation on a theme rearranges its material, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: Antonin Dvorak's initials are A and D

explanation.surface: A dimwit's attempt at a set of variations on a Dvorak theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variation on' rearranges A THEME into MEATHE. 'initially' gives the composer's two initials, not just D, which supplies the second A.
explanation.definitionFit: Meathead is slang for a dim, thick-headed person.

clue.text: Old composer's feeble part for violin, with final note changed

parts.note: pale can mean weak or feeble, as in a pale imitation

indicators.note: the last letter G is itself a musical note and is swapped for another note, A

parts.note: a string is part of a violin

explanation.surface: An old composer writes a weak violin part, altering the final note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with final note changed' swaps STRING's last letter G (a note name) for A, giving STRINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina was a sixteenth-century Italian composer of sacred music.

clue.text: Origin of material — of course, it's a variation

indicators.note: a variation reworks the original, so the word course is rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that the origin of some material is, naturally, a variation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's a variation' rearranges COURSE; 'of' is just a link that makes the surface read as 'of course'.
explanation.definitionFit: A source is where information or material comes from, its point of origin.

clue.text: Has turned around a variation's start with a new note, it's plain

indicators.note: around means the reversed word goes round the other letters
turned means the word has is read in reverse
start picks the first letter of the word variation's

explanation.surface: A melody turns round on a variation's opening, adding a new note to a plain tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses HAS to SAH, and 'around' puts AVANN inside it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A savannah is a grassy plain with few trees, typical of tropical Africa.

clue.text: In opera Tosca's an inspirational female

indicators.note: in says the answer lies inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: In Puccini's opera, Tosca is a heroine who inspires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the letters running across 'opera Tosca's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, goddesses who inspired artists and poets.

clue.text: Like successful disk from disheartened exponent of 24 down

indicators.note: disheartened means the word loses its heart, its middle letter

parts.note: Glenn Gould, the Canadian pianist, was a famous interpreter of Bach

explanation.surface: A hit record by a downcast Bach performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Gould's famous recordings were of Bach's Goldberg Variations; 'disheartened' removes the central U of GOULD.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold disc is the award for a record that sells in large numbers, so a successful one goes gold.

clue.text: A variation on theme in gruesome branch of mathematics

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the synonym for gruesome

parts.note: gory means bloody and gruesome

indicators.note: a variation on a theme rearranges it, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A musical variation on a theme turns up in something gruesome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gruesome' looks like it describes the mathematics, but it supplies the container; the anagram of A THEME sits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Game theory is the mathematical study of strategy and decision-making among competing players.

clue.text: More work coming from Martinu to pianist

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A new work by the composer Martinu is passed to a pianist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is Thomas More, not 'additional'; Martinu is a Czech composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is the famous book by Sir Thomas More describing an ideal island state.

clue.text: Provided tribute with adagio he composed about maiden, under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue under means the following letters come after the P

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the M
composed means the letters of adagio and he are arranged anew

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A composer pays tribute with an adagio about a young woman, written under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adagio' tempts as a tempo marking, but it is plain fodder for 'composed'; in a down clue 'under pressure' means the pressure letter heads the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay homage is to show public respect or give tribute, so paid homage means provided it.

clue.text: X-ray unit providing information on stricken tenor

indicators.note: in an across clue on means the information follows the reworked tenor
stricken suggests the word tenor is struck and knocked into a new order

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Information supplied on a tenor who has been taken ill, via an X-ray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stricken' looks like the tenor is ill, but it signals a rearrangement; 'on' in an across clue sets the information after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The roentgen is an old unit of radiation exposure, named after the discoverer of X-rays.

clue.text: Medley of airs around piano at home as way to ease pain

indicators.note: around means the mixed letters go round the P
a medley mixes tunes together, so the letters of airs are mixed

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
in means at home

explanation.surface: A medley of tunes played softly at home to soothe pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medley of' turns AIRS into ASIR; 'around' puts P inside it, giving ASPIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common painkiller taken to relieve headaches and other aches.

clue.text: Shut up about a theme's opening being undeveloped

indicators.note: about means the confining word goes round the other letters

parts.note: to immure is to wall up or imprison

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of theme's

explanation.surface: Keeping quiet about how a theme opens, being immature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' looks like a command to be quiet; here it means to wall in or imprison.
explanation.definitionFit: Immature means not fully grown or developed.

clue.text: Devoted enthusiasts did wrong, interrupting performances

indicators.note: interrupting means the rearranged letters break into the word for performances

parts.note: acts are performances, as in a variety bill

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters of did are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Fans behaved badly, disrupting the shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devoted enthusiasts' is the definition: fans can be called addicts, as in a crossword addict.
explanation.definitionFit: Addicts are devotees or fans, as in jazz addicts.

clue.text: Melody, not hard, I try with variation for brass

indicators.note: not means the letter for hard is left out

parts.note: a theme is a melody
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: with variation means the letters of I and try are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tune played without force, as I attempt a variation for brass instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes H from THEME, giving TEME; 'with variation' turns I TRY into RITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass in the informal sense is cheek or effrontery, the same as temerity.

clue.text: In middle of bad day study extra pieces

indicators.note: in puts the synonym for study inside the middle letters
middle of takes the letters between the first and last of the phrase

parts.note: a den is a private study or room

explanation.surface: Doing extra study on a bad day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes the inside of the two-word phrase 'bad day' as one run, not a letter from each word.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are items added to a book or document, the plural of addendum.

clue.text: Performed sacred music and theme inside

indicators.note: inside means theme sits within the word and

explanation.surface: Sacred music was performed, and the theme was included in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense is rare: anthem as a verb, to sing or celebrate in an anthem, is in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: To anthem is an old verb meaning to celebrate in song, so anthemed means sang a sacred anthem.

clue.text: Provides resolution to Beethoven's Ninth with arrangement of verse

indicators.note: ninth picks the ninth letter of the composer's name
a musical arrangement reworks material, so the letters of verse are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone resolves Beethoven's Ninth Symphony using a new setting of a verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beethoven's Ninth' is not the symphony but the ninth letter of BEETHOVEN, N; 'arrangement of' turns VERSE into ERVES.
explanation.definitionFit: To nerve someone is to give them courage or resolve.

clue.text: Composer of many variations has cultural snobs dropping in

indicators.note: dropping means the word in is let fall out of the longer word

parts.note: Brahmins, especially Boston Brahmins, are a socially and culturally superior elite

explanation.surface: A composer drops in, along with some cultural snobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes IN from BRAHMINS, a term for a highbrow social elite.
explanation.definitionFit: Brahms wrote several sets of variations, including those on themes by Haydn and Handel.

clue.text: Extraneous variation on theme included in otherwise bare disk

indicators.note: included in means one set of letters goes inside the other
otherwise means the letters of bare disk are put another way
a variation on a theme reworks it, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An irrelevant variation on a theme put on an otherwise empty record.
explanation.walkthrough: A B-side is the lesser track of a single, which suits the surface's 'disk'; 'otherwise' and 'variation on' each mix their own words before 'included in' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beside the mark misses the point, so it is irrelevant or extraneous.

clue.text: For variation on theme by us, work by Liszt

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: a variation reworks a theme, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Liszt writes a piece offering a variation on a theme of our own.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface picks up the puzzle's theme of variations; 'by' simply places the pieces next to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Prometheus is a symphonic poem by Franz Liszt, named after the Titan who stole fire.

clue.text: European composer looked up to by some Africans

definitions.meaning: Alban ... was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School

definitions.text: looked up to by some Africans
definitions.meaning: in South African usage a ... is a mountain, something one looks up at

explanation.walkthrough: Afrikaans and South African English use berg for a mountain, as in the Drakensberg range.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg wrote Wozzeck, and berg is the South African word for a hill or mountain.

clue.text: Single person, in short, who created 10 with other 24 variations

indicators.note: in short means the word is cut down, losing its tail

parts.note: a bachelor is an unmarried man

explanation.surface: An unmarried man, briefly, wrote some famous variations.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 across and 24 across together give GOLD + BERG, the Goldberg Variations; 'in short' cuts BACHELOR down to its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Sebastian Bach composed the Goldberg Variations, a set of thirty variations for keyboard.

clue.text: Talented young player who later scored in game, for example?

definitions.text: Talented young player who later scored in game, for example?

parts.words: Talented young player who later scored in game, for example?
parts.note: the composer was a gifted young violinist who later wrote music; scored means composed, and in game rearranged gives the title of his most famous set of variations

explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' looks like sport, but means wrote music for; 'in game, for example?' is a variation of the letters of the puzzle word at 3 down, the name of his famous work.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Elgar played the violin as a youth before composing the Enigma Variations.

clue.text: Offer as a tribute 1812, say, about European hero retreating

indicators.note: about means the date goes round the other letters

parts.note: 1812 is an example of a date, a year

indicators.note: retreating means the hero's name is read backwards

parts.note: El Cid is the great hero of medieval Spain

explanation.surface: Offering the 1812 Overture as a tribute to a European hero who retreated.
explanation.walkthrough: '1812' wants to be Tchaikovsky's overture, but here it is just a year, an example of a date; El Cid is the Spanish hero.
explanation.definitionFit: To dedicate a work is to offer it in honour of someone, as a tribute.
